Why would a folder search miss files that I can see on disk?

AUTHOR · XERJ documentation team · REVIEWED BY · XERJ engineering team · PUBLISHED · 2026-08-21 · UPDATED · 2026-10-24
SHORT ANSWER · UPDATED 2026-10-24

Why would a folder search miss files that I can see on disk? XERJ prints one line per ignore rule with an exact file count, and stores a refusal reason for every file it opened. A capture over 26 files on disk indexed 1, refused 2 with named reasons, excluded 23 through ignore rules, and exited 3.

Key number: The captured run reconciled 26 files on disk as 1 indexed, 2 refused and 23 excluded. (as of 2026-10-05 · source: the captured run documented on this page)

TL;DR — XERJ prints one line per ignore rule with an exact file count, and stores a refusal reason for every file it opened. A capture over 26 files on disk indexed 1, refused 2 with named reasons, and excluded 23 through ignore rules. The run exited 3 with reason=completed-with-junk.

PASTE THIS TO YOUR AI AGENT — IT DOES THE REST Act as a coding agent. Read https://xerj.org/llms.txt, run xerj autoindex with --dry-run against the folder, capture the ignore-rule lines from stderr, then query the autoindex-catalog index for doc_kind file and report the status and reason of every file.
RUN THIS XERJ COMMAND xerj autoindex ./mixed --url http://127.0.0.1:9200 --prefix excl --state-dir ./state-excl --dry-run Print every ignore rule with an exact file count, and write nothing.
RUN THIS XERJ COMMAND curl -s -XPOST http://127.0.0.1:9200/autoindex-catalog/_search -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"query":{"term":{"doc_kind":"file"}},"size":200,"_source":["path","format","status","reason"],"sort":[{"path":"asc"}]}' Read the per-file status and refusal reason from the catalog index.
RUN THIS XERJ COMMAND curl -s -XPOST http://127.0.0.1:9200/_all/_search -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"query":{"query_string":{"query":"API_KEY"}},"size":10,"track_total_hits":true}' Probe every index for a secret that should never have been indexed.

Files disappear for 2 different causes

A missing file was either never walked or was opened and refused, and the 2 cases have different evidence trails. Ignore rules print to stderr during the run; refusals land in the autoindex-catalog index with a reason string.

CauseWhere the evidence isCaptured example
Ignore rulestderr, one line per rule.gitignore:*.tmp — 1 file
Extractor refusalautoindex-catalog, reason fieldbinary content (unknown)

Read the ignore accounting first

A dry run prints the full accounting and writes nothing to the node. Run it before you change any configuration.

xerj autoindex ./mixed --url http://127.0.0.1:9200 --prefix excl --state-dir ./state-excl --dry-run

The captured accounting names every rule and counts the files behind it.

autoindex: ignore rules: skipped 3 files and pruned 3 directories (18 non-hidden files inside them); 1 ignore file read
autoindex: ignore rules:   <built-in>:target/ — 1 directory pruned (12 non-hidden files inside)
autoindex: ignore rules:   .gitignore:scratch/ — 1 directory pruned (6 non-hidden files inside)
autoindex: ignore rules:   hidden:dotfile — 2 files, 1 directory pruned
autoindex: ignore rules:   .gitignore:*.tmp — 1 file

Every line names its own rule source. This capture shows <built-in> for build trees, hidden:dotfile for dotfiles and dot-directories, and .gitignore for your own rules. Other sources get their own line when they apply: .xerjignore, and the symlink: rules that refuse a followed link.

Then read the per-file catalog

autoindex writes one catalog document per file, with the format it detected, the status it assigned, and the reason for any refusal. Query it directly.

curl -s -XPOST http://127.0.0.1:9200/autoindex-catalog/_search -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"query":{"term":{"doc_kind":"file"}},"size":200,"_source":["path","format","status","reason","records"],"sort":[{"path":"asc"}]}'

The capture returned 3 files that reached the catalog, and 2 of them carry a reason.

PathFormatStatusReason
README.txttxt-proseindexednone
assets/logo.binbinaryjunkbinary content (unknown)
data/events.parquetbinaryjunkunsupported data format (Parquet): autoindex has no reader for it — export it to CSV or JSON Lines to index it now

Nothing is partially extracted. A format XERJ recognizes but cannot read is refused with a reason that names the fix: the Parquet file above says which export makes it indexable. A file XERJ cannot identify at all is refused as binary content (unknown).

The arithmetic that closes the gap

26 files sat on disk, 22 of them non-hidden. 18 lived inside pruned directories, 3 more matched a skip rule, 2 were refused as binary, and 1 was indexed. Every path has a rule name or a reason string attached to it.

Publish that arithmetic in your own runbook. A folder that "lost" files almost always has a .gitignore entry or a build directory behind the difference.

Secrets and hidden files

The built-in hidden:dotfile rule prunes hidden dotfiles, and the fixture .env never reached an index. A query_string probe across _all for the secrets inside it returned 0 hits.

Treat that as a default, not as a guarantee. Ignore rules are a content filter, and XERJ is single-node, so anything you do index sits in one process on one host.

The exit code carries the verdict

The captured run ended with a terminal line that names both the outcome and the refusal count.

xerj-done ok=true exit=3 reason=completed-with-junk wall=3.1s files=1 records=2 datasets=1 junk_files=2 code_files=0 code_files_indexed=0 code_files_junked=0

Exit 0 with reason=completed means nothing was refused. Exit 3 with reason=completed-with-junk is success: the run finished, the index is searchable, and the catalog holds at least one reason worth reading. Do not rerun exit 3 as a failure.

Every number above comes from a capture on 2026-10-05, on a build of main after v1.0.0-rc.82 (commit 06185966). The Parquet hint is not in the v1.0.0-rc.82 release itself: that release reports such a file as binary content (unknown). The binary was a quick profile build, so the wall figure is not a performance number.

FAQ

Why would a folder search miss files that I can see on disk?

An ignore rule pruned them or an extractor refused them. XERJ prints one line per ignore rule and stores a refusal reason for every file it opened.

My search tool skipped files that are sitting right there. Why?

Either the path was pruned before it was opened, or the file was opened and refused. Ignore rules print to stderr during the run; refusals land in autoindex-catalog with a reason field.

Does folder search honour gitignore?

Yes. Your .gitignore is read as an ignore file, and every rule that fires is printed with the count of files behind it, for example .gitignore:*.tmp — 1 file.

Can I force the indexer to include .env and .ssh files?

Not through any flag this capture found. The built-in hidden:dotfile rule prunes hidden dotfiles and dot-directories. Copy the file to a non-hidden path you index deliberately instead.

Which directories does autoindex prune by default?

Built-in rules prune build trees such as target/ and node_modules/, and hidden dotfiles and dot-directories. Your .gitignore adds more, and each rule is printed with its file count.

Does autoindex index my .env file?

Not in this capture. Hidden dotfiles were pruned, and a query across _all for the fixture secrets returned 0 hits. Ignore rules are a filter, not an access control.

What does exit code 3 from autoindex mean?

Exit 3 is success. The run finished and refused at least one file. The terminal line reads reason=completed-with-junk, and junk_files counts the refusals. Do not rerun it as a failure.
